correctness.rationale: For every n>=5, the first, second and third admissible sets have sizes N=C(n,2), 2(n-2), n-2, respectively; memorylessness gives independent exponentials at these rates. The third winner is the unique triangle closure with probability 1/(n-2), otherwise fixes a star with n-4 remaining unit clocks. This proves the entire exact joint law; binomial and exponential identities yield the variance anomaly and the independent Exp(2)+Exp(1) and Gumbel limits. Exhaustive rational-state, successor geometry, and Laplace checks executed successfully in the delivered standalone checker for n=5..8. Finite code checks only supplement the all-n argument.

originality.rationale: The exact marked pair of output size and last-success time, its two conditional time scales and its variance/weak-convergence discrepancy were not located in targeted published-finding corpus queries, the accessible current-week source claims, or inspected primary papers. The closest rare-catastrophe result is about a different graph family, and the closest Kneser source treats an alternate dissociation invariant. The published RSA and local-limit papers state general models and distinct host regimes; the random Kneser EKR article studies percolation of incompatibility edges, not greedy arrival times. Priority is qualified by accessible-text limitations, not inferred merely from search failure.
residual_risks: Older complete texts on adsorption in highly symmetric finite graphs were not exhaustively accessible; the SIAM 1989 paper was only abstract-accessible.
Closest public published-finding corpus records were abstract-accessible, not full-text inspectable; other general greedy theories could contain an implicit stronger special case.
The elementary three-step branch makes historical independent rediscovery plausible; this audit is not a certification of publication priority.

value.rationale: KG(n,2) is the canonical rank-two Erdos-Ko-Rado graph and the probability model is the standard stochastic random greedy maximal independent-set algorithm. The theorem gives an exact algorithmic output/last-success-time law throughout an infinite natural graph family; it quantifies rare extensive suboptimality with exact probability 1/(n-2), distinguishes O(1/n) exceptional jamming from O(log n) typical jamming, and exhibits a concrete failure of second-moment convergence despite weak concentration. These are natural stability and kinetic questions, not a computation at a chosen arbitrary small parameter.
